correctness.rationale: For an internal perpendicular foot on edge i, its two positive acute radial angles are exactly arccos(h_i/d_i) and arccos(h_i/d_(i+1)), so their sum is the prescribed vertex-ray gap. Since f_h(d)=arccos(h/d) has derivative h/(d sqrt(d^2-h^2))>0, comparing two admissible solutions forces consecutive strict signs to alternate (or equality propagates around the cycle). Odd n forbids nonzero alternating comparisons. The log-radius Jacobian has only diagonal a_i=h_i/sqrt(d_i^2-h_i^2)>0 and cyclic-forward b_i>0; det J=product a_i+(-1)^(n-1)product b_i, positive for odd n. Analytic inverse-function theorem applies in the strict-foot open domain. Explicit even quadrilateral rays pi/4+k pi/2 with radii alternately sec t,csc t have all h_i=1 for t in (0,pi/2). Checked actual standard-library geometry script and independently evaluated cyclic Jacobians for odd n=3,5,7,9, plus direct nonuniform triangle and equal-support even family from the proof. Finite samples corroborate analytic argument, not prove it.
